related_questions.question: Is it safe to eat eggs bird flu in the UK?
related_questions.snippet: General advice to the public The Food Standards Agency has said that on the basis of the current scientific evidence, bird flu poses a very low food safety risk for UK consumers. Properly cooked poultry and poultry products, including eggs, are safe to eat. Avian influenza is unconnected with coronavirus (COVID-19).

related_questions.question: Can you eat eggs from chickens with bird flu?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is generally safe to eat eggs from chickens with bird flu, as long as the eggs are properly cooked. The risk of contracting bird flu from consuming eggs is very low because the virus is inactivated by heat.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is generally safe to eat eggs from chickens with bird flu, as long as the eggs are properly cooked

list.title: Cooking kills the virus:
list.snippet: Cooking poultry and eggs to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) will kill the H5N1 virus, as well as other viruses and bacteria, according to the New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services.

list.title: Rapid onset of symptoms:
list.snippet: Chickens infected with bird flu typically exhibit severe symptoms quickly, making them unlikely to lay eggs that make it into the food supply.

list.title: USDA safeguards:
list.snippet: The USDA has implemented measures such as flock testing and federal inspection programs to prevent infected poultry and eggs from entering the food chain.
Thoroughly cook eggs: Ensure that egg yolks are fully cooked and not runny.
Prevent cross-contamination: Keep raw poultry and eggs separate from cooked foods to avoid spreading bacteria or viruses.
Proper food handling: Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water after handling raw poultry and eggs.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while it's natural to be concerned about bird flu and its potential impact on food safety, properly cooked poultry and eggs remain safe to consume.
